newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian 97/98 rice exports looking weaker-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Australian 97/98 rice exports looking weaker-ABARE.

text.p: Australian 1997/98 (paddy) rice production is expected to match the record set in 1996/97 but both exports and grower returns may slip, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
In its June quarter bulletin, ABARE forecast production of 1.405 million tonnes (paddy) rice in the financial year to end June 1998 from an estimated 1.407 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Exports were forecast to slip to 790,000 tonnes from an estimated 797,000 in the current year, which was revised down from the 820,000 predicted in the March quarter bulletin.
Average grower returns were seen easing to A$194 a tonne in 1997/98 from A$197 a tonne, down from the A$200 forecast in the previous bulletin, the government advisory body said.

World rice trade was forecast to fall five percent to 17.2 million tonnes in 1997/98 from an estimated 18.1 million in the current year despite world consumption rising. "The weak import demand is expected to result from large rice harvests in many Asian countries in 1996/97," ABARE said. As a result world rice prices were expected to fall slightly, it said.
The agency said there was some reason to expect a rise in exports of Australian rice to Japan in the coming year.

"There are some prospects for an increase in Australian rice exports to Japan with an announcement in April 1997 that the timing of Japan's rice tenders would be adjusted to take account of Australia's harvest time," ABARE said.
"However, no concrete concessions were given to increase imports of Australian rice," it added.
Australian rice production in 1997/98 might have even been larger were it not for limits to receival facilities in the Riverina district and lower world prices, ABARE said.

The agency said that since rice production began in Victoria in 1996/97, significant investment had been undertaken in receival and storage facilities and output was expected to almost triple in 1997/89 to around 20,000 tonnes.

World production was forecast to rise 0.3 percent in 1997/98 to 378 million tonnes from an estimated 377 million in 1996/97, while consumption was seen up 0.8 percent to 379 million tonnes from 376 million this year, ABARE said.
